topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: Project Agora shows how tokenisation can improve wholesale cross-border payments; work will advance to real-value testing
key_claim: Project Agora demonstrated atomic settlement of wholesale cross-border transactions using tokenised central bank reserves and tokenised commercial bank deposits across seven jurisdictions, and will now advance to real-value testing with the Bank of Canada joining.
frame_summary: The BIS argues tokenisation can fix long-standing inefficiencies in wholesale cross-border payments while preserving the safety of central-bank-money settlement, moving the public-private prototype from concept toward real-value trials.
verbatim_quote: The project, involving the Bank of England, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, the Bank of France (representing the Eurosystem), the Bank of Japan, the Bank of Korea, the Bank of Mexico, the Swiss National Bank and more than 40 private sector financial institutions, today published a report detailing the findings of its exploratory work.

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: Tokenisation can improve wholesale cross-border payments: key findings from Project Agora
key_claim: The Eurosystem, comprising the ECB and the central banks of the 21 euro area countries, participated with more than 40 financial institutions in Project Agora, which showed atomic multi-currency settlement using tokenised reserves and tokenised commercial bank deposits and feeds the Eurosystem's Pontes and Appia initiatives.
frame_summary: The ECB argues that tokenisation and programmability can overcome the structural frictions of cross-border payments while preserving settlement integrity, and positions the work within Europe's drive for payments sovereignty.
verbatim_quote: The Eurosystem, comprising the European Central Bank (ECB) and the central banks of the 21 euro area countries, participates in Project Agora, which is run by the Bank for International Settlements and the Institute of International Finance, with leading central banks and more than 40 financial institutions.

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: Stablecoins in 2025: Developments and Financial Stability Implications
date_evidence: April 08, 2026  Stablecoins in 2025: Developments and Financial Stability Implications
key_claim: Stablecoin aggregate market capitalisation reached $317 billion as of April 6, 2026, more than 50 percent growth since early 2025, while complex intermediation chains, vertical integration and accelerating retail adoption introduce novel financial-stability vulnerabilities.
frame_summary: The Fed note argues that even as regulation brings stablecoins inside the perimeter, their deepening interconnection with traditional finance and opaque structures amplify run and contagion risk.
verbatim_quote: The stablecoin market has demonstrated significant growth in 2025, with aggregate market capitalization reaching $317 billion as of April 6, 2026, representing a more than 50% growth since early 2025, despite flattening-out during the final quarter of 2025 and first quarter of 2026.

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: Banks in the Age of Stablecoins: Lessons from Their Historical Responses to Financial Innovations
date_evidence: May 01, 2026  Banks in the Age of Stablecoins: Lessons from Their Historical Responses to Financial Innovations
key_claim: History shows banks recapture share lost to innovations rather than being passively disintermediated, attracting over $300 billion into money market deposit accounts within three months of their December 1982 authorization, implying banks will adapt to stablecoins.
frame_summary: The Fed note argues, through historical precedent, that banks actively adapt to financial innovations via advocacy, product innovation and partnership, so stablecoins will provoke competitive response rather than passive deposit flight.
verbatim_quote: Within just three months of their authorization in December 1982, banks attracted over $300 billion into these accounts, recapturing substantial market share (Keeley & Zimmerman (1985)).

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
publisher: White House Council of Economic Advisers
title: Effects of Stablecoin Yield Prohibition on Bank Lending
date_evidence: Effects of Stablecoin Yield Prohibition on Bank Lending  Council of Economic Advisers  April 2026
key_claim: Under baseline calibration the GENIUS Act prohibition on stablecoin yield raises bank lending by only $2.1 billion (0.017 percent of total loans), because the $300 billion stablecoin market is tiny against $17.15 trillion in deposits.
frame_summary: The CEA paper argues the macroeconomic stakes of the stablecoin yield ban are negligible, so the policy neither materially boosts nor harms bank credit supply.
verbatim_quote: The stablecoin market currently stands at roughly $300 billion (CoinMarketCap) against $17.15 trillion in total deposits (Federal Reserve Release H.8 Table 4, Line 34); At baseline, full prohibition generates a $2.1 billion lending gain (0.017% of total loans).

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
publisher: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
title: GENIUS Act: Reporting Forms and Instructions for Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers Subject to the Jurisdiction of the OCC (Bulletin 2026-24)
key_claim: The OCC proposes weekly (Form PS-01) and quarterly (Form PS-02) reporting for permitted and foreign payment stablecoin issuers registered under the GENIUS Act, operationalising the supervisory machinery behind its March 2026 proposed rule.
frame_summary: The OCC bulletin argues for building the prudential reporting infrastructure needed to supervise payment stablecoin issuers, formalising federal oversight of the new instrument.

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: GENIUS Act Requirements and Standards for FDIC-Supervised Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers and Insured Depository Institutions
date_evidence: A Proposed Rule by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation on 04/10/2026
key_claim: The FDIC proposes that deposits backing a payment stablecoin are insured to the issuer but not pass-through to stablecoin holders, and defines a significant redemption request as aggregate redemptions exceeding 10 percent of outstanding issuance within a single 24-hour period.
frame_summary: The FDIC rule argues for extending the deposit-insurance perimeter and prudential clarity to the stablecoin sector, bounding the safety net as stablecoins integrate with insured banks.
verbatim_quote: The FDIC would define "significant redemption request" to mean a circumstance in which aggregate redemption requests exceed 10 percent of a PPSI's outstanding issuance value within a single 24-hour period.

key_claim: The digital euro regulation (procedure 2023/0212(COD)) has the Council negotiating position adopted in December 2025 and ECON amendment negotiations underway, with rapporteur Navarrete distinguishing an offline tokenised-cash version from an online account-based version.
frame_summary: This neutral Parliament tracker documents the legislative progress of the digital euro file, showing it moving through Council and Parliament toward a committee vote.

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: Bank of England launches consultation on regulating systemic stablecoins (proposed regime, sterling-denominated systemic stablecoins)
key_claim: The Bank proposes a prudential regime for sterling systemic stablecoins with up to 60 percent of backing in short-term UK government debt and temporary holding limits of 20,000 pounds per coin for individuals and 10 million pounds for businesses.
frame_summary: The Bank of England argues for a robust financial-stability regime, jointly run with the FCA, to admit sterling systemic stablecoins without endangering trust in money or the supply of credit.
verbatim_quote: the Bank is proposing temporary holding limits of 20,000 pounds per coin for individuals and 10 million pounds for businesses (with an exemptions regime to allow the largest businesses to hold more if required).

title: Euro numerique : le temps de l'engagement commun
date_evidence: Tribune du Gouverneur de la Banque de France, Francois Villeroy de Galhau, et du Premier sous-gouverneur, Denis Beau, publiee dans Les Echos du 24 avril 2026 ; Mise en ligne le 24 Avril 2026
key_claim: The Banque de France leadership states the digital euro was approved unanimously by member states in December and backed by a large majority of the European Parliament in February 2026, with a final vote expected by summer and a pilot possible in the second half of 2027 for public rollout around 2029.
frame_summary: The Banque de France argues the digital euro is a sovereignty imperative, a digital banknote complementing private solutions, and urges French banks to engage now in the preparatory public-private work.
verbatim_quote: Si les negociations entre colegislateurs aboutissent cette annee, un projet pilote pourra etre lance au second semestre 2027, pour un deploiement aupres du grand public a l'horizon 2029.

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: How the stablecoins boom is reshaping the power of banks
key_claim: Even if stablecoin supply reached Citigroup's bullish $4 trillion by 2030, total supply would remain small against more than $72 trillion in projected global commercial deposits excluding China, so the near-term threat is fragmentation of banks' liquidity role rather than mass deposit flight.
frame_summary: Oliver Wyman argues stablecoins will pressure deposit funding costs and payment fees and open new fee revenue, but are unlikely to fully disintermediate banks, especially if banks issue competing tokenised money.
verbatim_quote: Even if stablecoin supply were to reach Citigroup's bullish scenario of $4 trillion by 2030, total supply would remain small compared with the more than $72 trillion in projected global commercial deposits (excluding China).

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: Tokenized Finance (IMF Note 2026/001)
key_claim: The IMF identifies three emerging types of tokenised money, tokenised commercial bank deposits, regulated stablecoins and wholesale CBDC, and warns that absent clear policy anchors tokenisation risks amplifying instability through speed, concentration and fragmentation.
frame_summary: The IMF Note argues tokenisation is a structural reallocation of trust toward shared infrastructures and programmable code, whose safety depends on anchoring in safe settlement assets, code governance, legal certainty and international coordination.
verbatim_quote: Three broad categories of tokenized money are emerging. Tokenized commercial bank deposits represent a digital extension of existing liabilities, retaining the two-tier monetary system while enhancing programmability.

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: JPMorganChase, Citi, other big banks push on-chain processing (The Clearing House token initiative)
key_claim: The Clearing House launched an initiative to clear and settle tokenized bank deposits across institutions including JPMorganChase, BMO, BNY, Citi, Citizens, Fifth Third, HSBC and Bank of America, layered onto its RTP and CHIPS networks, where CHIPS clears and settles $2.2 trillion daily.
frame_summary: American Banker argues a shared regulated clearing-and-settlement layer is the missing interoperability piece that will push fence-sitting banks to adopt tokenized deposits and keep next-generation rails under bank control rather than fintechs.
verbatim_quote: This includes TCH initiatives such as the RTP real-time payment network and the CHIPs private sector payments network that clears and settles $2.2 trillion daily.

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: The rumor of cash's death is greatly exaggerated (Fed data shows cash use holding steady)
key_claim: Federal Reserve Diary of Consumer Payment Choice data show consumers made an average of six cash payments a month in 2025, down from 14 in 2016 but not zero, and 76 percent of consumers carried cash, evidencing a slow rather than collapsing decline.
frame_summary: American Banker argues cash usage is declining only gradually and remains resilient, so banks will need to keep supporting it even as digital payments dominate.
verbatim_quote: Consumers made an average of six cash payments a month in 2025, and while that is down from 14 in 2016, it's not zero.

title: Qivalis grows to 37 banks ahead of euro stablecoin launch
key_claim: The Amsterdam-domiciled, MiCAR-compliant Qivalis consortium added 25 banks to reach 37 members (founders include ING, BNP Paribas, UniCredit), targeting a regulated euro-stablecoin launch in the second half of 2026, against USDT at $189.61 billion and USDC at $76.28 billion.

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: Yield-Bearing Stablecoins Can Destroy Deposits
date_evidence: BPI companion PDF index entry: Stablecoins Can Destroy Deposits, Bill Nelson, May 8, 2026
key_claim: The Bank Policy Institute argues yield-bearing stablecoins are near-perfect substitutes for deposits that destroy them dollar-for-dollar, estimating that if stablecoin adoption reaches roughly $4 trillion by 2030 it would result in $3.7 trillion in destroyed deposits and could cut lending by a fifth or more.
frame_summary: BPI argues against the view that deposits cannot leave the banking system, contending that yield-bearing stablecoins permanently shrink deposits and bank lending, a warning aimed at Congress and regulators.
verbatim_quote: if stablecoin adoption reaches roughly four trillion dollars by 2030, deposits would therefore decline, resulting in $3.7 trillion in destroyed deposits.

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: Mastercard launches Agent Pay for Machines to unlock super-fast, always-on payments
key_claim: Mastercard introduced Agent Pay for Machines, a service for permissioned, machine-speed, micro-value AI-agent payments with guaranteed multi-rail settlement across cards, accounts and stablecoins, with more than 30 launch partners including Adyen, Ant International, Coinbase and Stripe.
frame_summary: Mastercard argues that AI agents transacting autonomously at high velocity need a new class of always-on, low-value machine payments and that its network can supply the trust, credentialing and multi-rail settlement to scale agentic commerce.
verbatim_quote: More than 30 industry leaders, including Adyen, Ant International, BVNK, Checkout.com, Cloudflare, Coinbase, Getnet by Santander, Global Payments, Lovable, OKX, Stripe and Tempo, are among the first to leverage and support adoption.

topic: Financial Services and the Future of Money
title: Visa Announces New AI, Stablecoin and Token Innovations to Power Intelligent, Programmable Commerce at Visa Payments Forum
key_claim: At Visa Payments Forum 2026 Visa unveiled agentic-commerce and token tools and said it has moved stablecoins across VisaNet at an annualized run rate of approximately $7 billion as of March 2026 with more than 160 stablecoin-linked card programs, and will build a layer to turn bank deposits into programmable tokenized deposits.
frame_summary: Visa argues AI is transforming the front end of commerce and stablecoins the back end, positioning itself as the trusted platform connecting AI, programmable money and existing infrastructure so clients modernise without replacing systems.
verbatim_quote: Building on its first stablecoin settlement pilots in early 2025, Visa has moved billions of dollars in stablecoins across VisaNet, with an annualized run rate of approximately $7 billion as of March 2026.
